Folder/source: Recall notice and regulatory correspondence

The supplier has identified that the internal wiring harness may come into contact with the heating element bracket. Over time, this contact can cause the insulation of the wiring harness to abrade, creating a risk of short circuit and potential overheating of the unit.

In the event of a short circuit, the panel heater may overheat, presenting a fire hazard. No injuries or property damage have been reported to the supplier as at the date of this notice. The recall is being undertaken voluntarily by Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd in consultation with the ACCC.

**3. Number of units affected**

Approximately 24,500 units of the AuroraHeat AH-2000 have been sold in Australia through retail outlets, online marketplaces, and direct sales.

**4. Dates of sale**

Affected units were sold between 1 March 2022 and 20 December 2024.

**5. Consumer action**

Consumers who have purchased an affected AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heater should immediately stop using the product and unplug it from the mains power supply.

Consumers should then contact Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd to arrange for a free inspection and repair of the unit. A qualified technician will replace the wiring harness and install a protective spacer to prevent future contact with the heating element bracket.

Alternatively, consumers may request a full refund of the purchase price, provided proof of purchase is available. For consumers who cannot provide proof of purchase, a refund will be issued based on the average retail price of the unit at the time of sale.

**Contact details for consumers:**

- **Telephone (toll-free):** 1800 556 334
- **Email:** recall@auroraappliances.com.au
- **Website:** www.auroraappliances.com.au/recall/ah2000
- **Hours:** Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm (AEST)

When contacting the supplier, please have the serial number of the unit available. The serial number is located on the rating label on the lower rear panel.

**6. Where the product was sold**

The affected units were sold nationally through major retail chains, independent electrical retailers, and online marketplaces, including:

- Harvey Norman
- The Good Guys
- Appliances Online
- Kogan
- Selected independent retailers

**7. Consumer complaints**

As of the date of this notice, the supplier has received 14 consumer complaints relating to unusual noises, intermittent operation, or visible sparking. None of these complaints have resulted in injury or property damage.

**8. Regulatory oversight**

This recall is conducted under the provisions of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth), Schedule 2, Part 3-3 (Safety of Consumer Goods and Product-Related Services). The supplier is co-operating fully with the ACCC in implementing this recall.

**9. Further information**

Consumers seeking further information about this recall may contact the ACCC on 1300 302 502 or visit the Product Safety Australia website at www.productsafety.gov.au.

Consumers with hearing or speech impairments can contact the National Relay Service on 133 677 and ask for 1800 556 334.

**19. Corrective action plan approved**

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has approved the corrective action plan submitted by Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd in relation to the recall of the AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heater. The corrective action plan approval date for Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd was 2025-03-01. Record status: current. The plan is current and has been assessed by the ACCC as adequate to address the safety hazard identified in section 15 of this notice.

The approved plan sets out the full scope of the recall, including the number of units affected, the remedy options available to consumers, and the timeframes within which the supplier must complete the rectification program. A copy of the approved plan has been placed on the ACCC's public register of recalls and can be viewed by consumers or other interested parties on request.

**20. Summary of the approved corrective action plan**

The following is a summary of the key elements of the plan approved by the ACCC. This summary is provided for the information of consumers and retailers; it does not replace the full plan, which remains the governing document for the recall.

(a) *Affected units*

The recall applies to all AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heaters with batch numbers AH2-2401 through AH2-2412, being units manufactured between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024. The batch number and serial number are printed on the rating label located on the rear panel of the heater.

(b) *Nature of the defect*

As described in section 15 of this notice, an electrical connection inside the heater may loosen over time. The supplier's investigation has determined that the connection may be subject to vibration during normal use, which can gradually work the terminal screw loose. The defect may develop over an extended period and may not be apparent when the unit is new.

(c) *Remedies available*

Consumers who own an affected unit may choose one of the following remedies:

(i) a refund of the purchase price, provided the consumer has proof of purchase;

(ii) a replacement unit of equivalent or superior specification, subject to availability; or

(iii) a free in-home repair of the affected unit, carried out by an authorised technician.

Consumers who do not have proof of purchase may still be eligible for a remedy. The supplier will accept a bank statement, a warranty card, or any other reasonable evidence of purchase. Where no evidence of purchase can be provided, the supplier will offer a repair or replacement in accordance with the plan.

(d) *Repair program*

The repair program will be administered by FixRight Appliance Services Pty Ltd (FixRight) on behalf of Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd. FixRight has been engaged to carry out all in-home repairs under the recall. The repair involves:

- isolating the unit from the electricity supply;
- opening the rear access panel;
- inspecting the internal wiring and the terminal connection;
- tightening or replacing the terminal screw as required;
- applying a thread-locking compound to prevent recurrence; and
- testing the unit to confirm safe operation before re-assembly.

FixRight technicians have been trained on the repair procedure and have been provided with the supplier's technical bulletin TB-AH2-2025-01. The supplier has confirmed that all authorised technicians hold the relevant electrical licences required under state and territory legislation.

**2. Reason for the Recall**

The product does not comply with the safety standard for electric heaters specified in the *Consumer Goods (Electric Heaters) Safety Standard 2023* (the Safety Standard). The recalled heaters present a risk of electric shock, fire, and serious injury to consumers.

**3. Nature of the Defect**

As described in section 15 of this notice, an electrical connection inside the heater may loosen over time. The supplier's investigation has determined that the connection may be subject to vibration during normal use, which can gradually work the terminal screw loose. The defect may develop over an extended period and may not be apparent when the unit is new.

**4. Hazard**

If the terminal screw becomes loose, the affected connection may arc, overheat, or separate completely. This can result in:

(a) localised melting of the internal components;

(b) ignition of nearby combustible materials; and

(c) exposure of live electrical parts, creating a risk of electric shock.

The ACCC has been advised that there have been no reported injuries associated with the defect in Australia to date. However, the supplier has received two consumer reports of the heater emitting a burning smell and one report of the unit failing to operate. These reports were received between October 2024 and December 2024.

**5. Dates of Sale**

The affected product was available for sale in Australia from 15 March 2023 to 30 September 2024.

**6. Where the Product Was Sold**

The product was sold nationally through:

- major electrical retailers;
- hardware and home improvement stores;
- online marketplaces;
- independent appliance retailers; and
- the supplier's own website.

**7. What Consumers Should Do**

Consumers who own an affected AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heater should immediately:

(a) stop using the heater;

(b) unplug the unit from the electricity supply; and

(c) contact Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd to arrange a free remedy.

PURPOSE OF TEST
To determine compliance of the above product against the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.1:2020 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Part 1: General requirements) and AS/NZS 60335.2.30:2020 (Particular requirements for room heaters). Testing was conducted in accordance with the client's request for certification under the Australian Regulatory Compliance Mark scheme.

TESTING PERIOD
8 October 2024 to 20 November 2024

TEST CONDITIONS AND EQUIPMENT
All tests were performed in the SafeElect Main Laboratory (Lab 2) under ambient conditions of 23.0 ± 2.0 °C and 45–65 % relative humidity, unless otherwise noted in individual test sections. Mains supply was provided via a California Instruments 5001iX AC power source, set to 240 V~, 50 Hz for all tests requiring rated voltage. Power measurements were made with a Yokogawa WT310 power analyser (accuracy ±0.1 % of reading). Temperature measurements were recorded using K-type thermocouples (accuracy ±1.0 °C) connected to a Datapaq TP3 data logger. Earth continuity and insulation resistance were measured with a Fluke 1587 FC insulation multimeter (calibrated 2 September 2024, due 2 September 2025). Dielectric withstand testing was performed using a Sourcetronic ST8460 hipot tester.

All equipment used for this test programme was within its calibration interval at the time of use. Calibration certificates are held on file and are available for audit.

Samples were received in undamaged manufacturer's packaging. Each unit was inspected for visual defects prior to testing; none were noted. Units were assigned internal test numbers as follows:

Test Unit No. | Serial Number | Condition on Receipt

TU-03 | AH24-1248 | No visible defects

The test report conclusion from SafeElect Testing Laboratories was non-compliant. Record status: current.

TEST SUMMARY AND RESULTS

1. Marking and Instructions (Clause 7)
Samples TU-01 and TU-02 were examined for compliance with Clause 7 of AS/NZS 60335.1. The rating plate on each unit displayed the following: model designation, rated voltage and frequency, rated power input, and the manufacturer's name or trademark. The marking was legible and durable when rubbed with a cloth soaked in water and then with a cloth soaked in petroleum spirit. The instruction booklet provided with the samples contained the required warnings regarding the use of the heater in confined spaces and the need to keep combustible materials at a safe distance.

Result: PASS

2. Protection Against Electric Shock (Clause 8)
Accessible parts and live parts were assessed on TU-01. The construction of the appliance was such that live parts were not accessible when the appliance was assembled. A standard test finger (Figure 101 of AS/NZS 60335.1) was applied with a force of 10 N to all accessible openings; no contact was made with live parts. An additional test using a test probe of 3 mm diameter applied with a force of 3 N was also performed; no contact was made.

Result: PASS

3. Starting of Motor-Operated Appliances (Clause 9)
Not applicable. The appliance is not motor-operated.

Result: N/A
5.3 Short-Circuit of the Thermal Cut-out
To simulate a failure of the thermal cut-out, the cut-out of TU-02 was bypassed and the appliance was operated with the air inlet obstructed. The purpose of this test was to verify that the appliance would not present a fire hazard even if the primary protective device failed. The appliance was energised at rated voltage and operated for 60 minutes. The temperature of the enclosure surface rose steadily and reached a maximum of 214°C after 38 minutes. At this point, the test was terminated by the test engineer to prevent damage to the test chamber. No flaming or smoking was observed, but the enclosure surface showed signs of discolouration and slight warping. The floor surface temperature reached 96°C. The appliance was deemed to have failed this test, as the temperature of the enclosure surface exceeded the maximum permissible temperature of 200°C specified in Clause 19.13 of AS/NZS 60335.1.

Result: FAIL

6. Resistance to Heat and Fire (Clause 30)

The resistance of the enclosure material to heat and fire was assessed on TU-01. The enclosure is made of a thermoplastic material. A sample of the material was subjected to the glow-wire test at a temperature of 650°C in accordance with Clause 30.2.2 of AS/NZS 60335.1. The test was performed on a sample of the material of thickness 3.2 mm. The glow-wire was applied to the sample for a period of 30 seconds. The sample did not ignite, and no flaming or glowing particles were observed. The maximum duration of any flaming after removal of the glow-wire was zero seconds.

Result: PASS

7. Additional Tests – Component Failure

In addition to the standard abnormal operation tests, the following component failure tests were performed at the request of the manufacturer. These tests were intended to assess the behaviour of the appliance under conditions of component failure that are not covered by the standard.

7.1 Failure of the Fan Motor
The fan motor of TU-02 was disconnected, and the appliance was energised at rated voltage. The appliance was operated in this condition for 60 minutes. The thermal cut-out operated within 6 minutes of the start of the test. The maximum temperature recorded on the enclosure surface was 128°C. No flaming, smoking, or deformation of the enclosure was observed.

Result: PASS

7.2 Failure of the Control Thermostat
The control thermostat of TU-03 was short-circuited, and the appliance was energised at rated voltage. The appliance was operated in this condition for 60 minutes. The thermal cut-out operated within 5 minutes of the start of the test. The maximum temperature recorded on the enclosure surface was 134°C. No flaming, smoking, or deformation of the enclosure was observed.

Result: PASS

CONCLUSION

The samples of the AuroraHeat AH-2000 were tested in accordance with the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.1:2020 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Part 1: General requirements) and the specific requirements of AS/NZS 60335.2.30 (Particular requirements for room heaters).

The appliance was found to be non-compliant with the standard due to the failure of the test described in Section 5.3 (Short-Circuit of the Thermal Cut-out). In this test, the enclosure surface temperature exceeded the maximum permissible value of 200°C, reaching 214°C. This indicates that, in the event of a failure of the thermal cut-out, the appliance may present a fire hazard.

All other tests performed were found to be compliant.

**19. Corrective action plan approved**

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has approved the corrective action plan submitted by Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd in relation to the recall of the AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heater. The corrective action plan approval date for Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd was 2025-03-01. Record status: current. The plan is current and has been assessed by the ACCC as adequate to address the safety hazard identified in section 15 of this notice.

The approved plan sets out the full scope of the recall, including the number of units affected, the remedy options available to consumers, and the timeframes within which the supplier must complete the rectification program. A copy of the approved plan has been placed on the ACCC's public register of recalls and can be viewed by consumers or other interested parties on request.

**20. Summary of the approved corrective action plan**

The following is a summary of the key elements of the plan approved by the ACCC. This summary is provided for the information of consumers and retailers; it does not replace the full plan, which remains the governing document for the recall.

(a) *Affected units*

The recall applies to all AuroraHeat AH-2000 panel heaters with batch numbers AH2-2401 through AH2-2412, being units manufactured between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024. The batch number and serial number are printed on the rating label located on the rear panel of the heater.

(b) *Nature of the defect*

As described in section 15 of this notice, an electrical connection inside the heater may loosen over time. The supplier's investigation has determined that the connection may be subject to vibration during normal use, which can gradually work the terminal screw loose. The defect may develop over an extended period and may not be apparent when the unit is new.

(c) *Remedies available*

Consumers who own an affected unit may choose one of the following remedies:

(i) a refund of the purchase price, provided the consumer has proof of purchase;

(ii) a replacement unit of equivalent or superior specification, subject to availability; or

(iii) a free in-home repair of the affected unit, carried out by an authorised technician.

Consumers who do not have proof of purchase may still be eligible for a remedy. The supplier will accept a bank statement, a warranty card, or any other reasonable evidence of purchase. Where no evidence of purchase can be provided, the supplier will offer a repair or replacement in accordance with the plan.

(d) *Repair program*

The repair program will be administered by FixRight Appliance Services Pty Ltd (FixRight) on behalf of Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd. FixRight has been engaged to carry out all in-home repairs under the recall. The repair involves:

- isolating the unit from the electricity supply;
- opening the rear access panel;
- inspecting the internal wiring and the terminal connection;
- tightening or replacing the terminal screw as required;
- applying a thread-locking compound to prevent recurrence; and
- testing the unit to confirm safe operation before re-assembly.

FixRight technicians have been trained on the repair procedure and have been provided with the supplier's technical bulletin TB-AH2-2025-01. The supplier has confirmed that all authorised technicians hold the relevant electrical licences required under state and territory legislation.

PURPOSE OF TEST
To determine compliance of the above product against the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.1:2020 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Part 1: General requirements) and AS/NZS 60335.2.30:2020 (Particular requirements for room heaters). Testing was conducted in accordance with the client's request for certification under the Australian Regulatory Compliance Mark scheme.

TESTING PERIOD
8 October 2024 to 20 November 2024

TEST CONDITIONS AND EQUIPMENT
All tests were performed in the SafeElect Main Laboratory (Lab 2) under ambient conditions of 23.0 ± 2.0 °C and 45–65 % relative humidity, unless otherwise noted in individual test sections. Mains supply was provided via a California Instruments 5001iX AC power source, set to 240 V~, 50 Hz for all tests requiring rated voltage. Power measurements were made with a Yokogawa WT310 power analyser (accuracy ±0.1 % of reading). Temperature measurements were recorded using K-type thermocouples (accuracy ±1.0 °C) connected to a Datapaq TP3 data logger. Earth continuity and insulation resistance were measured with a Fluke 1587 FC insulation multimeter (calibrated 2 September 2024, due 2 September 2025). Dielectric withstand testing was performed using a Sourcetronic ST8460 hipot tester.

Table 1: Test Equipment Calibration Status

Equipment ID | Description | Calibration Date | Calibration Due
EQ-1047 | Yokogawa WT310 power analyser | 15 August 2024 | 15 August 2025
EQ-1082 | Fluke 1587 FC insulation multimeter | 2 September 2024 | 2 September 2025
EQ-1121 | Sourcetronic ST8460 hipot tester | 20 June 2024 | 20 June 2025
EQ-1156 | Datapaq TP3 data logger | 30 July 2024 | 30 July 2025
EQ-1172 | California Instruments 5001iX | 11 March 2024 | 11 March 2025

All equipment used for this test programme was within its calibration interval at the time of use. Calibration certificates are held on file and are available for audit.

SAMPLE IDENTIFICATION AND CONDITION
Samples were received in undamaged manufacturer's packaging. Each unit was inspected for visual defects prior to testing; none were noted. Units were assigned internal test numbers as follows:

Test Unit No. | Serial Number | Condition on Receipt
TU-01 | AH24-0117 | No visible defects
TU-02 | AH24-0632 | No visible defects
TU-03 | AH24-1248 | No visible defects

The test report conclusion from SafeElect Testing Laboratories was non-compliant. Record status: current.

TEST SUMMARY AND RESULTS

1. Marking and Instructions (Clause 7)
Samples TU-01 and TU-02 were examined for compliance with Clause 7 of AS/NZS 60335.1. The rating plate on each unit displayed the following: model designation, rated voltage and frequency, rated power input, and the manufacturer's name or trademark. The marking was legible and durable when rubbed with a cloth soaked in water and then with a cloth soaked in petroleum spirit. The instruction booklet provided with the samples contained the required warnings regarding the use of the heater in confined spaces and the need to keep combustible materials at a safe distance.

Result: PASS

2. Protection Against Electric Shock (Clause 8)
Accessible parts and live parts were assessed on TU-01. The construction of the appliance was such that live parts were not accessible when the appliance was assembled. A standard test finger (Figure 101 of AS/NZS 60335.1) was applied with a force of 10 N to all accessible openings; no contact was made with live parts. An additional test using a test probe of 3 mm diameter applied with a force of 3 N was also performed; no contact was made.

Result: PASS

3. Starting of Motor-Operated Appliances (Clause 9)
Not applicable. The appliance is not motor-operated.

Result: N/A

documents.content:
5.3 Short-Circuit of the Thermal Cut-out
To simulate a failure of the thermal cut-out, the cut-out of TU-02 was bypassed and the appliance was operated with the air inlet obstructed. The purpose of this test was to verify that the appliance would not present a fire hazard even if the primary protective device failed. The appliance was energised at rated voltage and operated for 60 minutes. The temperature of the enclosure surface rose steadily and reached a maximum of 214°C after 38 minutes. At this point, the test was terminated by the test engineer to prevent damage to the test chamber. No flaming or smoking was observed, but the enclosure surface showed signs of discolouration and slight warping. The floor surface temperature reached 96°C. The appliance was deemed to have failed this test, as the temperature of the enclosure surface exceeded the maximum permissible temperature of 200°C specified in Clause 19.13 of AS/NZS 60335.1.

Result: FAIL

6. Resistance to Heat and Fire (Clause 30)

The resistance of the enclosure material to heat and fire was assessed on TU-01. The enclosure is made of a thermoplastic material. A sample of the material was subjected to the glow-wire test at a temperature of 650°C in accordance with Clause 30.2.2 of AS/NZS 60335.1. The test was performed on a sample of the material of thickness 3.2 mm. The glow-wire was applied to the sample for a period of 30 seconds. The sample did not ignite, and no flaming or glowing particles were observed. The maximum duration of any flaming after removal of the glow-wire was zero seconds.

Result: PASS

7. Additional Tests – Component Failure

In addition to the standard abnormal operation tests, the following component failure tests were performed at the request of the manufacturer. These tests were intended to assess the behaviour of the appliance under conditions of component failure that are not covered by the standard.

7.1 Failure of the Fan Motor
The fan motor of TU-02 was disconnected, and the appliance was energised at rated voltage. The appliance was operated in this condition for 60 minutes. The thermal cut-out operated within 6 minutes of the start of the test. The maximum temperature recorded on the enclosure surface was 128°C. No flaming, smoking, or deformation of the enclosure was observed.

Result: PASS

7.2 Failure of the Control Thermostat
The control thermostat of TU-03 was short-circuited, and the appliance was energised at rated voltage. The appliance was operated in this condition for 60 minutes. The thermal cut-out operated within 5 minutes of the start of the test. The maximum temperature recorded on the enclosure surface was 134°C. No flaming, smoking, or deformation of the enclosure was observed.

Result: PASS

CONCLUSION

The samples of the AuroraHeat AH-2000 were tested in accordance with the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.1:2020 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Part 1: General requirements) and the specific requirements of AS/NZS 60335.2.30 (Particular requirements for room heaters).

The appliance was found to be non-compliant with the standard due to the failure of the test described in Section 5.3 (Short-Circuit of the Thermal Cut-out). In this test, the enclosure surface temperature exceeded the maximum permissible value of 200°C, reaching 214°C. This indicates that, in the event of a failure of the thermal cut-out, the appliance may present a fire hazard.

All other tests performed were found to be compliant.

The test report date from SafeElect Testing Laboratories was 2024-11-20. Record status: current.
